content: TAF12, also known as Transcription Initiation Factor TFIID Subunit 12, is a protein encoded by the TAF12 gene in humans. It plays a critical role in the regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II. Transcription control involves a fundamental set of proteins collectively referred to as the basal transcription machinery. These proteins, together with RNA polymerase II, form complexes that are influenced by transactivator proteins. These transactivators bind to specific DNA sequences known as cis-regulatory elements, which are located near the transcription start site. Some of these transactivator proteins directly interact with the basal transcription complex, while others act as intermediary or bridging proteins, connecting transactivators to the basal transcription factors. Within the TFIID complex, certain associated factors are loosely bound, whereas others are tightly integrated with the TATA-binding protein (TBP). Among the tightly associated factors are the TAF (TBP-associated factor) proteins. Different TAFs are thought to facilitate the activity of specific transcriptional activators, enabling the regulation of various gene promoters and RNA polymerases. TAF12 is one such TAF protein and is known to interact directly with TBP as well as with another TAF protein, TAF2I. In terms of molecular interactions, TAF12 has been demonstrated to interact with TAF9, another TBP-associated factor, and with the transcription initiation protein SPT3 homolog. These interactions highlight its role in the assembly and function of the transcriptional machinery.
